components.gap: C003: two claims of the required Durrett presentation (p. 87) are not on the route: (i) the Section 2.5.1 opening claim that an advantage of the random-series proof of the strong law is that it gives estimates of the rate of convergence of S_n/n -> mu; (ii) the Remark's conclusion that, by comparison with the law of the iterated logarithm limsup S_n/(n^{1/2}(log log n)^{1/2}) = sigma sqrt(2) a.s., the rate of Theorem 2.5.11 is 'not far from the best possible'. The routed boundary (lines 303-312) reports only the LIL formula and says the logarithmic factor is not declared optimal, without Durrett's assessment. Supply both claims. components.gap: C010: the claims with which Durrett introduces Theorem 2.5.13 (p. 88) are not on the route: (i) the St. Petersburg motivation that EX_i = infinity and S_n/(n log_2 n) -> 1 in probability while limsup S_n/(n log_2 n) = infinity a.s. Supply these claims, with proofs of the mathematical consequences in (i) and (iii).
